summary.headline: FY26 revenue fell to INR 660.6 crore from INR 1,291.9 crore and Q4 Gross Profit turned negative at INR -6.1 crore as domestic lounge model reset.
summary.overview: FY26 was a transition year: domestic lounge volumes fell after banks shifted from unlimited to spend-based lounge access, cutting consolidated revenue roughly in half. Adjusted EBITDA fell to INR 25.0 crore from INR 102.1 crore and PAT to INR 11.6 crore from INR 65.1 crore. Q4 FY26 was loss-making at the gross profit, EBITDA and PAT level. Management pointed to global lounges (transaction volumes up 140% YoY), the Ten11 Hospitality railway lounge acquisition, the ongoing ETT acquisition and B2C membership (DreamFolks Club 2.0) as the growth drivers. Management said FY27 would be a transition year with breakeven possibly about a year later.

segments.name: Domestic airport lounges
segments.commentary: Previously more than 90% of revenue; structural reset from unlimited to spend-based access drove the FY26 decline. Management said the business is now largely new in nature. Management did not give a quantified split.

segments.name: Global lounges
segments.commentary: Transaction volumes grew 140% YoY, and the network covers over 1,000 airport touchpoints. Clients onboarded in Southeast Asia, with Middle East work ongoing. Management did not disclose revenue for this segment.

segments.name: Railway lounges
segments.commentary: Acquired Ten11 Hospitality in November 2025, giving direct control of premium railway lounges. Operational at Chennai, Mumbai and Vadodara; Lucknow expected soon. Management reiterated an INR 500 crore revenue target over 5 years and said at least 50 lounges are needed to reach that scale.

segments.name: Lifestyle services and B2C
segments.commentary: New lifestyle services include spa, social clubs, room upgrades, app-based airport transfers, star-hotel meals and mall coffee. DreamFolks Club 2.0 B2C membership launched about 5-6 months ago, with spend kept deliberately modest.

guidance_outlook: FY27 described as a transition year; management said breakeven could come about a year later, not by year-end.
Railway lounge INR 500 crore revenue target over 5 years reiterated, conditional on railway station modernisation and lounge count rising to at least 50.
Global lounge volume growth expected to keep accelerating; management asked investors to judge on a 2-year horizon rather than near-term numbers.
Management expects a swift recovery in travel once Middle East airspace restrictions ease.
A premium services program for global banks and card networks in South-East Asia is in advanced stages and expected to open a new revenue stream.
capex_capacity: Ten11 Hospitality acquisition completed November 2025; railway lounges operational at Chennai, Mumbai and Vadodara, with Lucknow expected soon.
ETT (Easy To Travel) acquisition is ongoing, adding international distribution and Middle East reach.
Management said the global lounge network is still being built out and more lounges are being onboarded before global client scaling.
Management described B2C investment as paced to revenue and not at full throttle.
demand_pricing: Industry-wide shift from unlimited lounge access to spend-based access and banks moving to lifestyle-oriented benefits reduced volumes in FY26.
Middle East conflict and airspace restrictions weighed on passenger traffic in FY26.
Global lounge volumes up 140% YoY; a marquee international client programme started in May 2026.
Receivables were about INR 130 crore at 31 Dec 2025; management said collections after 31 March 2026 had reduced this substantially, with no current figure given.
Management said it is focused on deepening existing bank relationships and selling lifestyle services into existing integrations.

qa_highlights.question: Given no international deals since listing, how confident is management of winning Middle East or South-East Asia clients?
qa_highlights.answer: Sandeep Sonawane cited 140% global lounge volume growth and said many clients were already onboarded, though he would not name them. Liberatha Kallat said network coverage and technology were built first and client acquisition has now started.

qa_highlights.question: When will the INR 130 crore receivables come down, given about INR 100 crore of revenue in the last two quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Shekhar Sood said dues at 31 Dec 2025 were significant but collections after 31 March 2026 have reduced them to a large extent. No updated number was given.

qa_highlights.question: How confident is management of reaching INR 500 crore railway revenue in 5 years, given low per-passenger revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Sandeep Sonawane said railway growth depends on station modernisation, that India has far fewer railway lounges than China or Russia, and that at least 50 lounges are needed to reach scale. The INR 500 crore target is still intact.

qa_highlights.question: What traction is there from the recently issued B2C cards?
qa_highlights.answer: Sandeep Sonawane said B2C started about 5-6 months ago with encouraging early numbers, but investment is being kept in line with revenue and the company is not going full throttle.

qa_highlights.question: What is the run-rate and year-end outlook, given the current INR 50 crore a quarter run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Sandeep Sonawane declined to give a year-end number and asked investors to focus on growth percentage and a 2-year view. He said global growth is accelerating monthly.

qa_highlights.question: Will breakeven be reached by year-end?
qa_highlights.answer: Liberatha Kallat said FY27 is a transition year and breakeven would likely come about a year later.

risks_watch: Domestic lounge revenue reset continues; management gave no quantified split of the domestic business or its revenue trajectory.
Q4 FY26 gross profit, EBITDA and PAT were all negative; FY27 breakeven timing is now guided about a year later.
Global client wins are not named or quantified; management said contracts will be announced when signed.
Railway growth depends on third-party station modernisation timelines and lounge count rising to at least 50.
Receivables of about INR 130 crore at 31 Dec 2025 need to be confirmed as collected.
Middle East conflict and airspace restrictions could delay the global recovery.
The ETT acquisition is still in progress; completion timing, consideration and financial impact were not discussed.
summary.management_tone: Candid and defensive on near-term numbers: management called FY26 transformational and conceded FY27 is a transition year with breakeven pushed out. It was confident on global growth and the railway target, but evasive on specific client wins, year-end run-rate and receivables.
key_quotes: FY26 has been a transformative year in DreamFolks' history — one that tested our resolve, challenged our operating model, and ultimately, sharpened our strategic focus.
So for FY '27, I will be very upfront that it's a transition time right now for us.
So we need to have -- we should be having not less than 50 lounges for us to really, really bring that scale and have that momentum and multiplying factor.

adds.what: Railway lounges at Chennai, Mumbai and Vadodara operational (Ten11 Hospitality); Lucknow expected soon; at least 50 lounges needed for INR 500 cr target

growth.why: FY27 is guided as a transition year with breakeven pushed out about a year; the INR 500 crore railway lounge target over 5 years is reiterated but conditional on station modernisation and at least 50 lounges, with no quantified near-term growth guidance, so backing is vague.
